item.title: Chelsea make Xabi Alonso sack decision after Leeds United humiliation at Stamford Bridge
item.description: Chelsea FC v Leeds United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Xabi Alonso is facing the first major crisis of his Chelsea tenure after a humiliating 4-1 home defeat to Leeds United sparked a furious reaction from the Stamford Bridge faithful. Despite the growing unrest, the Blues hierarchy have delivered a definitive verdict on the Spaniard's immediate future in the dugout. Chelsea hierarchy resist panic after dismal Leeds collapse Saturday's 4-1 defeat against bitter rivals Leeds ended the visitors' 27-year wait for a Premier League win in west London. Loud boos echoed around the stadium at full-time as frustrated supporters voiced their anger. That setback marked a third loss in four league matches, leaving Chelsea stuck in mid-table and short on belief. Alonso's side have suffered five defeats overall while conceding an alarming 20 goals in 11 games. Yet according to Mail Sport , club executives will not make a hasty call to dismiss the 44-year-old. Despite his honeymoon period ending abruptly, boardroom figures are unwilling to pull the trigger so early in his reign. Why Stamford Bridge chiefs are backing their summer coup Luring Alonso this summer was viewed as a major coup. Chelsea beat Liverpool and Manchester City to the former Real Madrid boss' signature while both rivals hunted replacements for their outgoing managers. Heavy investment fuelled title expectations, especially without European football as a distraction. "When we won games, when we lost games, we always said that no matter what, it’s a process," he added. item.title: USC caps perfect homestand with big win over Louisiana
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- It wasn't as flashy as the first two games of No. 18 USC's homestand, but they got the job done nonetheless. The Trojans improved to 6-0 with an 82-56 victory over the Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns on Sunday night at the Galen Center, led once again by the talented backcourt duo of Rodney Rice and Alijah Arenas. The pair combined to lead USC in scoring, totaling 36 on 50% shooting. Both guards dropped 18, with Rice dishing out a game-high six assists and snagging three rebounds in the process. Meanwhile, Arenas added two assists of his own. Their combined 18-for-21 mark from the free-throw line helped provide a nice padding throughout the evening. "I thought [Rice] was phenomenal, and so was Alijah. We were +33 with Alijah on the floor...so some really good stuff there in our backcourt for sure," said head coach Eric Musselman. While the duo has certainly been a success thus far, Musselman admitted that there was uncertainty surrounding how they might produce together on the floor. "Sometimes when you have returning players, you have a feel. But they never played one second together," he said. "There's a risk that we talked about internally as a staff; we talked about it a little bit with them as well, how to make it work. I don't see a backcourt that's playing better than them..." Arenas headed into Sunday's contest with his 22 points per game ranked second in Big Ten scoring, fueled by a 57.8% shooting display through the first five games of the season. After going 4-of-9 in the victory, he has now shot at least 44% in every single game. It was the Ratliff twins, however, that helped kickstart an early run for the Trojans. Adonis opened the scoring with a pair of free throws before collecting a steal a few plays later, which led to a four-point play from Darius. Their six quick points came as part of a 10-0 USC run to begin the contest. Both continued to add on steadily throughout the night, finishing in double-digit scoring and getting it done on the defensive end as well. Darius finished with a career-high 17 points, adding six rebounds, three assists and a steal. He also earned a game-high four blocks, imposing his will against the driving attack of Louisiana. item.title: WRU to discuss Anglo-Welsh move at crucial summit
item.description: Welsh Rugby Union president Terry Cobner, chief executive Abi Tierney and new chair Lyndon Faulkner all spoke at the AGM [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Welsh Rugby Union chief executive (WRU) Abi Tierney says the prospect of Welsh clubs joining an expanded English league will be discussed in January at a crucial two-day summit meeting. The event, which has been delayed after initially being planned for December, will include the WRU, regions and external stakeholders - with plans to cut a Welsh professional men's side also to be discussed. "The summit is critical and we're creating it together," said Tierney, speaking after the WRU annual general meeting (AGM) at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. "It is everything. We'll have all the owners and their boards in a room, all the data and facts on the table, and we'll be saying, this is what it tells us." The WRU announced they hope for both internal and external speakers, with three key areas set to be focused on; financial and commercial, pathways and performance, and what it takes to win. Anglo-Welsh options emerge but URC issues remain Tierney admitted the recent prospect of trying to get into an Anglo-Welsh league will be discussed in January. Rugby Football Union (RFU) chief executive Bill Sweeney confirmed earlier in November that the WRU had officially asked to join the English Prem and form an Anglo-Welsh league. The Prem hopes to expand from 10 to 12 teams for the 2029-30 season, with a "long-term ambition" to grow further. Prem Rugby has opened a registration process for teams to apply, with a 'request for information stage' now open until 1 February 2027 and which Welsh sides will now consider applying for. Tierney was careful about what she said as she addressed the issue for the first time. "Clearly, there's been a significant change in something that wasn't there a year ago that we've got to now take into account," she said. "When we originally did the consultation last year, Anglo-Welsh wasn't an option. We tested it at the time and were told it wasn't an option. "We've always said through this process that if other things change and options become available, it's beholden on us to explore all options. "We've got a lot of water to go under the bridge to figure out what that combination is." That includes discussions on continued involvement in the United Rugby Championship (URC), the five-country, cross-border competition to which the WRU is committed to providing four sides until 2028. The WRU are a stakeholder in the competition alongside other member unions from Scotland, Ireland, Italy and South Africa. "The relationship with the URC continues to be constructive," said Tierney. "We're talking to them regularly. I think they understand on a human and inter-relational level. We continue to work as we always have." item.description: Morgan Guilavogui (9) before assisting Solans in the first goal of the match. | Real Salt Lake Real Salt Lake Captain Rafael Cabral had another brilliant night as the Brazilian goalkeeper made five crucial saves that kept the Wasatch side from falling behind early on. Quotable “We have to get more rotations, we have to move the ball across the back line quicker and we have to get the ball to the outside backs so we can move up the field faster to attack.” — Head coach Pablo Mastroeni on what he thought the back line could do better. Game summary The contest started out slowly as both sides looked for an opening in the opposition defense to find an early opening goal. Vancouver created the best chance of the opening 15’ as Whitecaps striker Bryan White found himself in a pocket of space inside the Real Salt Lake penalty area. Experienced defender Lukas Engel slid over from the left side to make a crucial block to deny the home team an early lead. The Canadian side came close to scoring the first goal of the match after a beautiful bicycle kick that almost found the top corner of the net if not for a headed clearance made by Philip Quinton. RSL had a golden opportunity to take the lead following a breakaway from Rookie striker Sergi Solans, the Spanish-born attacker saw his effort parried away by the Vancouver goalkeeper. The initial clearance was smashed into the feet of Saba Lobjanidze, whose shot forced Yohei Takaoka into making another important save. A minute before the end of the first half, a deep cross found the foot of Édier Ocampo, who cannoned a one-time strike into the roof of the net for the opening goal of the game. Vancouver doubled its lead following chaos in the Real Salt Lake penalty box, multiple rebounds that found the feet of the Whitecaps players. The Utah defenders threw their bodies at the ball before a big deflection save made by Cabral, clawing the ball away from the mouth of his goal. The Canadian-based team was able to dig out a dangerous cross that found the head of Bruno Caicado, who was wide open in the middle of the six-yard box to make it 2-0. The Whitecaps came close to making it three after Caicado had a curling effort that was denied by the strong left hand of Cabral. On the ensuing corner, Caicado found himself wide out in the middle of the six-yard box for a second time. His header was powered toward the ground but another brilliant save from Cabral using the right side of his body to keep the game within striking distance.

item.title: Jamie Carragher admits he 'felt sorry' for Man Utd star and slams Mauricio Pochettino's 'bizarre' decision in Liverpool thrashing
item.description: Manchester City FC v Wolverhampton Wanderers FC - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Jamie Carragher has admitted he "felt sorry" for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s humiliating 4-0 defeat at the hands of Liverpool on Sunday. The former Reds defender questioned Mauricio Pochettino's "bizarre" decision to throw the Dutchman into such a high-intensity environment for his first start of the season. Ten-man United crumble in Pochettino's first match Pochettino endured a nightmare start in the United dugout as Liverpool ran riot at Anfield. The contest swung inside 13 minutes, beginning when Leny Yoro received a straight red card before the 10-minute mark for halting Alexander Isak's clear run on goal. Dominik Szoboszlai punished the visitors from the resulting free-kick before Florian Wirtz doubled the lead from Rio Ngumoha's cross. Having assisted the second, 18-year-old England international Ngumoha scored after the break before Victor Munoz added a fourth late on. Carragher questions De Ligt selection Speaking on Sky Sports , Carragher questioned Pochettino's call to hand De Ligt his first start of the campaign. "I thought it was a really strange decision," Carragher said. "It was such a bizarre decision. Not because of his quality because I think he’s a better centre-back than Harry Maguire when you look at what he’s achieved in his career and the clubs he’s played for. "But he hasn’t played football so to play him at Anfield away, it felt so wrong. He was all over the place. It got to the stage where I was actually feeling sorry for him and I was actually pleading with the manager to take him off and take him out of the firing line. "He’s played for some top football clubs - Bayern Munich, Ajax and Juventus - those are some of the biggest clubs in the world. So to watch him perform like that… I felt sorry for him." Relegation pressure mounts on struggling Red Devils Defeat at Anfield compounds a dismal Premier League campaign that leaves United 19th with just eight points from 11 matches. Asked about their precarious table position, captain Bruno Fernandes admitted the squad must spark their own turnaround. "It’s very painful and it hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation," he said. Despite conceding four goals after Yoro's dismissal, the midfielder praised his team-mates' spirit under pressure. "You want to get results, but today it was not possible for us. There were a lot of things we can look at and I saw a lot of character from the team," Fernandes continued. "The result won’t show that but I am very proud of everyone in the dressing room." item.description: Celtics Loss To Warriors Marks First Four-Game Losing Streak Since 2021 originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Boston's West Coast Trip has not been kind to Joe Mazzulla's crew. The Celtics went into Sunday coming off a horrific loss to the 1-14 Sacramento Kings , needing a bounceback performance to end the weekend on a high note. Instead, Jayson Tatum and company put up a season-low in points, dropping an 88-87 contest to a Stephen Curry-less Warriors team. The loss was the team's fourth in a row, their first slump of four consecutive games since May 12, 2021. The streak is over. A week after beating Dallas by 37, the Celtics lose four straight by a combined 16 points. They go to Washington Tuesday trying to avoid their first five-game losing streak in 11 years. https://t.co/rh1pBMVKPt — Sean Grande (@SeanGrandePBP) November 23, 2026 Tatum led the way with 27 points on 8-of-20 shooting, adding 10 rebounds and six assists. item.title: What NFL had to say about controversial call that took critical touchdown from Jaguars in loss to Giants
item.description: New York Giants cornerback Dru Phillips (22) defends against Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) on Nov. 22, 2026, in Brooklyn, N.Y. The football world is abuzz over the no-touchdown call on a fourth – quarter pass to Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington in Sunday’s game against the Giants. While it appeared that Washington had made the catch in the end zone with the Jaguars trailing the Giants 20-6 at the time, the officials ruled it an incomplete pass and confirmed the call after a video review. The Giants went on to win the game 23-18 . New York Giants cornerback Dru Phillips (22) defends against Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) on Nov. 22, 2026, in Brooklyn, N.Y. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST Everyone from Washington to the fans to CBS Sports rules analyst Gene Steratore all believed that Washington had control of the ball. “I did not think he lost possession of the football. … I think it’s a touchdown, fellas,” Steratore said during the broadcast. "I did not think he lost possession of the football … I think it's a touchdown fellas." @GeneSteratore disagrees with the call of INCOMPLETE after review pic.twitter.com/b2T3eoe5my — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) November 23, 2026 However, the NFL did not agree. In an interview with a pool reporter, NFL VP of instant replay Mark Butterworth said Washington did not have full control of the ball. “The ruling on the field was an incomplete pass,” Butterworth said. “First, to overturn a call, we need clear and obvious video evidence to overturn the on-field ruling. It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds.” In follow-up questions, he confirmed that he was referring to the fact that when Washington hit the ground, the ball was moving in the Jaguars receiver’s hands. item.title: NFL Punishes Three Falcons Players for Incidents During Chiefs Game
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs v Atlanta Falcons Getty The NFL has fined three Atlanta Falcons players for incidents during the Week 10 game against the Kansas City Chiefs. This weekend, the NFL announced that it has fined DL Brandon Dorlus, DB DeMarcco Hellams, and LB Harold Perkins. Dorlus was fined $7,114 twice for separate incidents (taunting and a late hit); Hellams was fined $6,509 for a hit on a defenseless player, and Perkins was fined $5,203 for use of the helmet. Dorlus’ incidents occurred in the fourth quarter. The first happened at 11:03 when he hit Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes during a second-down play. The second happened with 5:18 remaining after Mahomes threw an incomplete pass. Dorlus was penalized for the hit on Mahomes but not for taunting. The incidents involving Hellams and Perkins happened in the second quarter. The officials did not penalize either player during the game. Falcons Last in NFC South, but Still in Playoff Race The Falcons lost to the Chiefs 35-13 and are now 3-7. They did not have a game this weekend, as they were one of six teams that were on a bye. While Atlanta has struggled this season, the team still has a chance to make the playoffs. The Falcons are in last place in the NFC South but just two games behind the Carolina Panthers, who lead the division. If the Falcons miss the playoffs, it would be the ninth consecutive season they would not participate in the postseason. It would be the longest playoff drought since 1983-1990. Falcons WR Jahan Dotson Reacts to NFC South Battle “I’ve never been in a situation where we’re one game out of the division with that record,” Falcons WR Jahan Dotson said last week, per Daniel Flick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . “But we are. That’s the circumstances that we’re dealt with right now. So, we have a perfect opportunity to come out of this bye week and make our mind up as to what we want to do as a football team. “I think we have the guys in this locker room to make this thing right, finish the season strong, and find ourselves in the postseason.” After finishing 8-9 last season, the Falcons made changes to the coaching staff and front office. Kevin Stefanski was hired as head coach, and Ian Cunningham was brought in to be the general manager. The Falcons also created a new position, president of football, and former Falcons QB and 2016 NFL MVP Matt Ryan was hired for the role. item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-LIVERPOOL-MAN UTD - AFP Rio Ngumoha etched his name into Liverpool history with a record-breaking display in their 4-0 demolition of Manchester United, yet the 18-year-old insists he must remain "grounded". Stepping up at a rocking Anfield, the teenage winger registered both a goal and an assist to inspire a nightmare debut for new Red Devils manager Mauricio Pochettino. Teenager makes Premier League history at Anfield At 18 years and 85 days old, Rio Ngumoha broke two long-standing Premier League records held by Michael Owen during Liverpool's emphatic win over Manchester United. He became the Reds' youngest league scorer in this fixture, surpassing Owen's 1998 mark, and the youngest Liverpool player to score and assist in a top-flight game since Boxing Day 1997. Ngumoha struck after the break from a Bradley Barcola pass, having already set up Florian Wirtz in the first half. His decisive display came after referee Sam Barrott sent off United defender Leny Yoro before the interval for a last-man foul on Alexander Isak. Ngumoha vows to stay grounded after 'special' display Speaking to BBC Match of the Day after the final whistle, the Chelsea academy graduate played down the growing attention around his performance and stressed that team success comes first. "Liverpool-United can't really get much bigger in my eyes," the 18-year-old said. "To get the three points here at Anfield is special. It was a really important game today. These records are really special and just getting goals and helping my team is the main thing, to get three points. Hopefully I can score and assist many more. "I just like exciting other people really, when I show everyone what I can do and get everyone off their seats. Hopefully I can keep going and keep my head on the floor and stay grounded." item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy.
